content.text:
I renamed `NamespaceBundle.getNamespaceObject()` to `getNamespaceName()` and updated the callers whose receiver is a `NamespaceBundle`. That is 33 call sites in 8 files, all in `pulsar-broker/src/main`. They are in `ServiceUnitStateChannelImpl`, `TransferShedder`, `DefaultNamespaceBundleSplitStrategyImpl`, `NamespaceService`, `PulsarService`, `BrokerService`, `SystemTopicBasedTopicPoliciesService` and `NamespaceBundleFactory`. Nothing was compiled, as requested.

`NamespaceBundle` implements `ServiceUnitId`, whose `getNamespaceObject()` is also implemented by `TopicName` and `NamespaceName`. A pure rename would stop `NamespaceBundle` implementing that interface method and break compilation. So in `NamespaceBundle.java` I kept an `@Override getNamespaceObject()` that delegates to the new `getNamespaceName()`. Call sites whose static type is `ServiceUnitId` still use `getNamespaceObject()`. These are in `LoadManagerShared`, `ModularLoadManagerImpl`, and the `ServiceUnitId`-typed helpers in `NamespaceService` (`findRedirectLookupResultAsync`, `checkHeartbeatNamespace`, `getSLAMonitorBrokerName`, `isHeartbeatNamespace`). All `TopicName` and `NamespaceName` usages are untouched. I picked the receivers by reading declared types in the source, so the build is the real check. If it flags anything, a missed `NamespaceBundle` caller will still compile through the delegate.
